entries.title: New Chat UX, Default-On Composer, New Cursor Tab Model
entries.titleJa: Cursor 0.40系: 新Chat UX、Composer標準化、新Tabモデル
entries.titleEn: New Chat UX, Default-On Composer, New Cursor Tab Model
entries.summaryJa: Cursorはバージョン0.40系で新しいチャットUXを導入し、Composer機能をデフォルトで有効化した。さらに新しいTab補完モデルを搭載し、編集体験とコード提案の精度を向上させている。
entries.summaryEn: UPDATE (0.40.1–0.40.4): Fixes a bug with apply on remote ssh, a few chat bugs, speeds up Cursor Tab for Europe/Asia users, fixes some outstanding Cursor Tab bugs and notifications hiding the chat inpu
entries.bodyJa:
AIネイティブのコードエディタCursorが、0.40系アップデートで主要機能を刷新した。新しいチャットUX、Composerのデフォルト有効化、そして新しいCursor Tabモデルが目玉となる。

チャットUXの再設計では、コードベースとの対話をより滑らかに行えるようインターフェースが整理された。Composerは複数ファイルにまたがる編集を一括で行える機能で、これまではオプトイン的な扱いだったが、本リリースでデフォルト有効となり、エージェント的な編集フローが標準体験に組み込まれた形だ。

さらに、コード補完の中核を担うCursor Tabモデルが新世代に更新された。Cursor TabはGitHub Copilotのインライン補完に相当する機能だが、カーソル位置だけでなく直近の編集履歴を踏まえた予測的なジャンプ・書き換え提案を行う点が特徴で、今回のモデル更新により提案の的中率や文脈追従性が改善されたと見られる。

背景として、AIコーディング領域はGitHub Copilot、Codeium(現Windsurf)、Replit Agent、JetBrains AI Assistantなどが競合し、近年は単発補完からマルチファイル編集や自律的タスク実行へと軸足が移っている。CursorのComposerデフォルト化は、この「エージェント的IDE」への業界的潮流に沿った動きと言える。Anysphere(Cursor開発元)は独自モデルとフロンティアモデル(Claude、GPT系)の組み合わせで差別化を図っており、Tabモデルの自社強化は推論コストと体験品質の両面で重要な投資領域となっている可能性がある。
entries.bodyEn:
Cursor, the AI-native code editor developed by Anysphere, has shipped its 0.40.x line with three headline changes: a redesigned chat UX, Composer enabled by default, and a new in-house Cursor Tab completion model.

The chat UX rework tightens how developers converse with their codebase inside the editor, smoothing the path between asking a question, reviewing diffs, and applying changes. While the changelog is terse, the direction is consistent with Cursor's broader push to make AI assistance feel like a first-class part of the editing surface rather than a side panel afterthought.

Composer, Cursor's multi-file editing mode, is now on by default. Previously positioned as an opt-in power-user feature, Composer lets the assistant plan and apply coordinated edits across several files in a single flow — closer in spirit to an autonomous coding agent than a traditional chat assistant. Making it the default signals that Anysphere views agentic, multi-file editing as the baseline expectation for its users, not an experimental mode.

The third change is a new Cursor Tab model. Tab is Cursor's predictive completion system, conceptually similar to GitHub Copilot's inline suggestions but extended to predict next edits and cursor jumps based on recent activity, not just the current caret position. A new model generation is likely to translate into better acceptance rates, fewer distracting suggestions, and tighter coupling with the user's editing trajectory, though the changelog does not publish benchmarks.

For context, the AI coding tools space has matured rapidly. GitHub Copilot remains the incumbent, while Codeium (now operating as Windsurf with its own agentic editor), Replit Agent, JetBrains AI Assistant, and open-source contenders like Continue and Aider have all pushed beyond single-line autocomplete into multi-file refactors and task execution. Cursor's decision to default Composer on, and to keep investing in a proprietary Tab model rather than relying solely on third-party APIs, fits this trajectory: the differentiator is increasingly the orchestration layer and the small, fast, edit-specialised models that sit alongside frontier LLMs like Claude and GPT.

There is also a strategic dimension worth noting. Running a custom completion model in-house gives Anysphere more control over latency, cost, and the specific behaviour of suggestions — all of which matter when a feature fires on nearly every keystroke. As frontier model providers continue to raise the bar on reasoning quality, the competitive frontier for AI editors may well shift toward this kind of editor-native infrastructure, with chat and Composer riding on top.
